Results.ReviewText:
Bought this to replace a gas grill I've had since 1995 (seriously). Before that my parents had a Weber kettle charcoal grill. I bought it at a store, so I was able to see the display model in person before buying it. I got the Mocha color (perhaps that chain's exclusive color as I don't see it listed on the Weber site). I went slow putting it together...took about 2-2 1/2 hours. The instructions are quite well done. The metal frame pieces are a bit flimsy (had to bend a few corners back in place while assembling), but the frame is more structurally sound once together. Overall I'm pleased with the assembly part. 

Like I mentioned this is my first new grill since 1995, so perhaps some of the features I found great are now industry standards. First up the cooking grate, which isn't one big piece but actually 2 pieces side by side. In all the pictures you see the grates with somewhat wide bars. But, you can flip them over and the other side has a narrower bar on top (the bars are shaped like a triangle so wide on one side, narrow on the other). The manual mentions this, but it's not seen in website photos. So, you could have a grate with more surface area on one side of the grill and flip the other grate to have more space between the bars on the other side. 

The other great feature deals with the gas tank. The tank hangs on the side, below the right shelf, and is very easy to install and replace. Hang the tank on the hook and then clamp down the guard (so no, the tank can't accidentally fall off while rolling the grill across the patio). But, the hook is also an indicator for the amount of gas still in the tank, which is measured by the weight of the tank. This is a great feature. So far I think it's pretty accurate...will see how it is as I use up tank and replace it. Again, this is mentioned in the manual but not shown on the website. 

Last, the left shelf folds down. This is nice for storage, and would be helpful for people using the grill in smaller spaces. These are just some of the features I found to be nice that weren't really highlighted.

Now, I did just find a 2 minute Weber YouTube video that mentions some of these features. Search Weber's videos for "Spirit II Features & Benefits" on YouTube and hopefully you'll find it. 

So cooking, how does it do? Like I said this replaced a grill I've used since 1995 which was barely working (couldn't even control temperature settings), so anything would be better than that one was. The separate temperature controls for the two burners are great. I like the thermometer on the lid. The starter has worked well so far (and does require a AA battery, which is included). I did not buy the iGrill for it, but perhaps in the future just to try it...I don't know why you'd need the iGrill unless you're lazy checking your food or you haven't ever grilled before and don't know what you're doing. I'm looking forward to using this grill more. I like the 10 year warranty on all parts as well (be sure to register your grill after purchase). I just laugh after all these years I'm back to a Weber grill.
Results.Title: Some of the best features aren't even mentioned

44010001.Name: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
44010001.Description:
Open the door to the world of grilling with crazy good food and friends coming together. Equipped with the powerful GS4 grilling system, this two burner gas grill is your entry to the Weber family and to everyday grilling. The compact open-cart design and the practical folding side table makes it fit even on small spaces, and you have all the basics you need to get familiar with gas grilling. So whether it’s a busy Monday or a relaxed Sunday – invite a couple of friends over, push the ignition and enjoy the special atmosphere that surrounds the grill.


 This product requires assembly.
